edges.description: Sarcomere paucity and impaired titin-mediated biomechanical support lead to chamber dilation and progressive loss of left ventricular systolic performance under load.
Progressive left ventricular systolic dysfunction and adverse chamber remodeling drive earlier onset of clinical heart failure and end-stage pump decompensation.
Chamber dilation, wall thinning, and elevated myocardial wall stress establish an arrhythmogenic substrate predisposing to sustained ventricular tachycardia.
Progressive left ventricular chamber dilation and reduced ejection fraction manifest clinically as dilated cardiomyopathy.
Severely impaired left ventricular systolic function progresses to symptomatic congestive heart failure and end-stage pump failure.
Increased wall stress and myocardial substrate remodeling in TTNtv-positive DCM confer a marked excess risk of sustained ventricular tachycardia.

nodes.description: Titin is the molecular ruler and elastic backbone of the sarcomere: it templates myofibril assembly, provides the passive restoring force of diastole, and transduces mechanical strain into signalling at the Z-disc and M-band. Human left-ventricular RNA and protein studies show biallelic TTN expression without substantial nonsense-mediated decay, while human TTNtv iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes exhibit a paucity of sarcomeres, suggesting that contractile force may be impaired directly through sarcomere loss; both haploinsufficiency of full-length titin and truncated-peptide effects remain under investigation.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion in CMD1G is a titin truncating variant (TTNtv) - a nonsense, frameshift, splice-disrupting, or copy-number change predicted to substantially alter the full-length titin polypeptide. Position and cardiac exon inclusion (percent spliced in, PSI > 90%) are the critical determinants of pathogenicity: disease-associated TTNtv are located predominantly in constitutively expressed exons of the inextensible A-band, the segment that binds myosin and myosin-binding protein C and is critical for biomechanical sensing and signaling. This positional and isoform-usage dependence separates pathogenic truncations from benign truncations in low-PSI exons found in the general population.

nodes.description: Chronic sarcomeric insufficiency produces the defining structural remodeling of dilated cardiomyopathy: progressive left ventricular chamber enlargement with wall thinning, myocyte loss, and interstitial/mid-wall fibrosis, accompanied by falling ejection fraction. Unlike the hypertrophic sarcomeropathies, the geometric response is dilation rather than wall thickening, and neurohormonal activation drives the remodeling forward.
